<h1 id="Paper-013-%E2%80%94-Ecological-Theory-in-Evolutionary-Computation">Paper 013 — Ecological Theory in Evolutionary Computation<a class="anchor-link" href="#Paper-013-%E2%80%94-Ecological-Theory-in-Evolutionary-Computation">¶</a></h1><p><strong>Dolson, E.D. &amp; Ofria, C.</strong> (2018). <em>Ecological Theory Provides Insights about Evolutionary Computation.</em> In <em>Proceedings of the Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference Companion (GECCO ’18 Companion)</em>, pp. 105–106.</p>
<p><strong>Summary.</strong> Evolutionary algorithm populations behave like ecological communities: we expect <strong>competitive exclusion</strong> when resources are effectively single-niched, <strong>niche partitioning</strong> that sustains diversity when multiple fitness peaks exist, and <strong>frequency-dependent selection</strong> when fitness depends on how crowded each niche is.</p>
<p>Adapted from <code>control/eco_dynamics/eco_dynamics.py</code>.</p>
<p>Provenance: <code>src/provenance/experiments.rs</code> — <code>ECO_DYNAMICS_PROVENANCE</code></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Background">Background<a class="anchor-link" href="#Background">¶</a></h2><p>Dolson and Ofria argue that viewing an EA population as an <strong>ecological community</strong> clarifies empirical patterns: genotypes compete for implicit “resources” encoded in the fitness landscape; multiple niches allow coexistence; frequency-dependent feedback can reward rare types and maintain diversity.</p>
<p><strong>BarraCUDA connection (GPU mapping).</strong> Population fitness evaluation parallels batch linear algebra (many genotypes scored together). Selection resembles tournament or softmax-style reductions over fitness. Diversity metrics such as Shannon entropy decompose into logarithms and sums over genotype frequencies—familiar reduce patterns on accelerators.</p>
</div>
</div>

<h3 id="Key-findings">Key findings<a class="anchor-link" href="#Key-findings">¶</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>Competitive exclusion:</strong> one effective niche plus strong selection drives convergence toward a dominant genotype.</li>
<li><strong>Niche differentiation:</strong> multiple Gaussian niches create multiple attractors, supporting higher diversity and lower monopoly by one genotype.</li>
<li><strong>Frequency-dependent selection:</strong> crowding reduces crowding-sensitive fitness, giving rare niche associations a relative edge and sustaining diversity.</li>
<li><strong>Productivity:</strong> more niches increase the ceiling of attainable mean population fitness under the same mutation and selection regime.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="ecoPrimals-mapping">ecoPrimals mapping<a class="anchor-link" href="#ecoPrimals-mapping">¶</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>Primals</strong> ↔ species or morphs in the computational community</li>
<li><strong>NUCLEUS</strong> ↔ habitat carrying resource structure (cores, memory, scheduling)</li>
<li><strong>biomeOS</strong> ↔ ecosystem-scale management of evolving primal populations</li>
</ul>
